messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Calculating McDonald's omega using info from MIRT
parts:
Hi Cathy,

McDonald's ω terms are marginal reliability estimates for the composite scores, assuming a constant standard error of measurement (SEM) for all potential score observations, whereas in IRT models are intended to reflect varying degrees of SEM as a conditional function of the θ input. Hence, estimates of marginal reliability after initially fitting a conditional reliability IRT model feels a lot like taking a step backwards. 

That said, if you want to do this for general reporting it is possible given different estimators in the package, some of which I discuss here. For further clarification, if you fit IRT models with non-constant slopes (e.g., 2PL) then these estimators work similarly to ω, whereas if you fit models with constant slopes (i.e., Rasch models) then they behave more like coefficient α, highlighting that α is really a (model) constrained version of ω (the τ-equivalence assumption manifest in the model directly). HTH.

Phil
